title: Lease Term Agreement Terms — Writing a Term and Accepting a Renewal Offer
content:
These terms govern how a Lease Term Agreement is written: its length, its end date, its start, its contracted rent for a new lease, and the acceptance of a renewal offer line.

## Article 1 — Length and end date

1.1 A term is written for a whole number of months between the term program's shortest and longest term (a month-to-month agreement runs one month at a time).

1.2 Its end date follows the program's end-date rule: the day before the same day number falling the term's months after the start date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day number does not exist.

## Article 2 — New-lease terms

2.1 A new-lease term starts on the move-in date, which must fall within the program's new-lease start window of calendar days after the lease approval.

2.2 Its contracted rent is the quoted 12-month monthly rent of the apartment home adjusted by the term program's rent adjustment, rounded half up to the cent; when the rent adjustment is a premium, the premium is at least the program's minimum monthly premium.

*Worked example (hypothetical).* A quoted 12-month rent of 1,600.00 dollars on the Flexible Lease (6-9 Months) program, whose adjustment is a premium of 8 percent with a minimum monthly premium of 75.00 dollars: 8 percent of 1,600.00 is 128.00, which is not below 75.00, so the contracted rent is 1,728.00 dollars. On a quoted rent of 900.00 dollars, 8 percent is 72.00, below the minimum, so the premium is 75.00 and the contracted rent is 975.00 dollars.

## Article 3 — Renewal terms

3.1 A renewal term starts on the day after the expiring term's end date and is written only from a renewal offer line of the expiring term.

3.2 **Offer still open.** A renewal may be signed only when the current date is no later than the offer date plus the offer's validity days. Offer validity days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the offer date, and the offer can be accepted through the last counted day. The offer date is the delivery date on the offer line record, and the validity days are those of the expiring term's program.

| Hypothetical offer line: delivered 1 May, open 30 days | Result |
|---|---|
| Counted days | 2 May through 31 May |
| Signing on 31 May (the last counted day) | May be signed |
| Signing on 1 June | May not be signed — the offer is no longer open |

3.3 *Retired clause.* The clause "its contracted rent is the offered rent of the accepted line, less the early renewal discount of the accepted term program when the resident signs at least that program's early renewal window before the expiring term end date" is **no longer in force**, together with the early renewal rent it defined (the offered rent less the early renewal discount); it has been superseded by the current basis for the contracted rent of a renewal.

3.4 A renewal is not signed while the lease has a past-due balance when the expiring program requires renewal only with no past-due balance.

## Article 4 — Start of a term

A term moves from pending to current on its start date, and for a new-lease term only once move-in is recorded.
